records.reason: Novel heavy diiodoaromatic scaffold at 20/1 and 100 ul. Its nonpolar, donor-free structure tests whether the compact predicted regime transfers to an uncovered molecule.
Paired novel m157 measurement at 1/1 and 150 ul. The same-molecule contrast supplies a solvent-strength response anchor for a scaffold absent from the labeled set.
Zero-EA-strength baseline for the novel fluorinated brominated arene m155. This expands coverage of donor-free halogenated structures with little polar functionality.
Same m155 scaffold and mobile phase at 150 ul. Comparing it with the 50-ul selection separates a possible loading association from structure-only behavior.
Novel nonpolar diaryl scaffold at 50/1. It tests whether the model's compact retention regime generalizes across a rigid hydrocarbon-like molecule without heteroatom interactions.
Low-strength PE anchor for the small nonpolar bromide m52. It provides coverage outside the carbonyl-rich families dominating recent failure repair.
Higher-strength, lower-volume m52 companion to the selected 0/1 row. The pair tests whether a simple nonpolar scaffold shows the expected condition response.
Novel chlorotoluene-like molecule under zero-EA-strength PE conditions. It probes retention for a simple donor-free halogenated aromatic environment.

Novel bulky halogenated aryl ether at 5/1. The single accessible acceptor and high molecular weight test whether heteroatom and halogen effects are being transferred too broadly from carbonyl compounds.
Novel polyaryl bromide at 20/1 and high loading volume. This high-CW-distance point tests size and aromaticity effects in a donor-free scaffold where a compact prediction is plausible but untested.
Novel iodophenol-like molecule at 10/1. Its hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor environment gives a distinct test of hydroxyl-containing retention behavior.
Nitrobenzaldehyde-like acceptor-rich structure at 5/1. It tests whether corrections learned from long-tail carbonyl and nitro-containing rows transfer to a distinct aldehyde environment.

Low-strength, low-volume anchor for carbonyl-rich m13. Observed m13 spans 4.51/10.63 at 0/1 and 53.01/93.28 at 10/1, 50 ul (bc2a96424966b655227f; c4bb286978fe9078a303); this point locates the onset of the steep response.

Weak-eluent m58 point tests transfer within a hydroxyl-containing scaffold. Observed m58 already ranges from 8.83/14.98 at 10/1, 50 ul to 27.23/45.56 at 50/1, 50 ul (aafc5710406e440a4c8f; 6b8fefaf0647d2239858).
Aldehyde-family anchor for m142 at 5/1. It extends the measured weak-eluent structure coverage beyond diketones and beta-ketoesters and tests positional-substitution transfer.

Difluorobenzaldehyde at 10/1 and 100 ul. Together with the measured m185 2/1 point (f3a9b0a4924369149487) and high-strength m185 point (c32500e81a05cfd2273d), it constrains the aldehyde response slope.

Low-volume m72 point at 5/1. The observed m72 long-tail values at 20/1 include 47.00/119.37 at 50 ul and 39.13/119.43 at 100 ul (8e7636d7a60a6058305a; 754f1d33b0ed61557754); this tests where the tail begins.
m102 ester at 10/1 and 100 ul. It adds an intermediate weak-eluent ester point to compare with the measured 50/1 result of 15.34/29.36 (ede97e1f4b6e7fe9a7eb).
Low-strength amino-benzoate point for m89. It complements the higher-strength measured m89 point at 10/1, 100 ul (c6a55a8d89f33c69899b) and tests onset of the amino-ester response.

Lower-strength anchor for m25. Measured m25 rises from 16.94/39.22 at 20/1, 150 ul to 33.94/89.38 at 50/1, 150 ul (0af9d219be9872711215; 74701496b6fc5465eea7); this fills the lower part of that curve.
m75 at 10/1 and 100 ul, an intermediate point between the measured 5/1 and 20/1 regimes. It tests whether the large loading-dependent and ratio-dependent changes persist at a third loading.
Low-strength m75 anchor at 1/1 and 100 ul. It helps distinguish a smooth response from the abrupt behavior seen between measured m75 rows at 50 ul and 150 ul.
Adjacent 2/1 m75 point at the same 100-ul loading. The matched 1/1, 2/1, and 10/1 selections directly test local response curvature under the loading regime where no measured anchor is available.

Low-ratio, low-volume m203 anchor. It contrasts with measured m203 20/1 values of 37.76/44.96 at 50 ul and 31.00/34.93 at 150 ul (9ed7c1fb1c2cc499bbf9; 66747ae127e03516ffda), probing onset and interval formation.
m203 at 20/1 and 100 ul tests transfer across loading between the measured compact 150-ul finish and the later 50-ul finish. This is a direct discriminator of endpoint-specific loading effects.

Independent m92 EA replicate at 20/1 and 100 ul. The PE and EA 1/1 records differ substantially, while EA records themselves vary; this tests whether the solvent association survives at higher strength and volume.

Independent lower-strength m92 EA replicate at 2/1 and 100 ul. Paired with the 20/1 EA row, it provides a local EA response curve while accounting for the variability seen in 00a89de0e6cc7377a84b, e626b5b8083ea1fd02f2, and 95a3dcfe4436e929aa30.

Independent m81 measurement at 10/1 and 100 ul. Measured m81 10/1 records show short finishes but meaningful variation (7d402b3fad455f06fe68; 390d6dfe33afc329fb17; 57646b9484b03f4076bb), so this tests loading transfer without assuming determinism.
Low-strength m51 anchor at 1/1 and 50 ul. The measured fixed-loading rise from 18.92/28.63 at 5/1 to 37.67/57.93 at 10/1 (bf09d868ed4d68a97b40; 4fb92bd1fab3ba235858) needs lower-ratio calibration.
Adjacent 2/1 m51 point at the same loading as the 1/1 selection. Together they test whether the observed tertiary-alcohol response begins smoothly or changes sharply before 5/1.
Low-strength m94 point at 1/1 and 150 ul. It anchors the steep beta-ketoester response below the measured 5/1 and 20/1 points (5b445b457a8b897a2d6c; e3a799d0fa90b649a157).

m95 at 10/1 and 150 ul tests loading transfer across a broad finish response. Relevant measured anchors are 13.90/32.26 at 10/1, 100 ul, 22.73/48.12 at 20/1, 50 ul, and 24.39/76.31 at 50/1, 100 ul (45e24a16b44a89653e4b; f402144b8672dd5ab2ab; 1a55639d058c08a1a06e).

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent sensitivity is strongly scaffold and structural-environment specific. Carbonyl-rich, aldehyde, ester, nitrile, and aromatic systems can show large retention growth, while structurally similar or less interactive compounds remain compact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The retrained model needs graph-condition interactions that prevent large corrections learned from long-tail carbonyl scaffolds from spreading to compact molecules.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which lower-strength anchors identify the onset and curvature of the remaining aldehyde, ester, diketone, and beta-ketoester response surfaces?

hypotheses.content: m75 and related scaffolds show loading-dependent, endpoint-dependent, and potentially nonmonotonic recorded responses. The m75 20/1-to-50/1 direction differs between 50-ul and 150-ul measurements.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Three m75 points at a common 100-ul loading can teach whether the apparent reversals are a reproducible interaction or isolated variation, improving condition-response generalization.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 100 ul, does m75 follow a smooth 1/1-to-10/1 response, and does its finish remain distinct from its onset response?

hypotheses.content: Loading associations are scaffold and endpoint dependent. m81 repeatedly shows short finishes in several high-loading or intermediate conditions, but identical or adjacent inputs still vary enough to limit a deterministic loading rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A further m81 point tests whether the retrained model should learn a transferable short-finish loading association or mainly represent residual variation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m81 at 10/1 and 100 ul retain the short finish seen in several 10/1 and 150-ul observations?

hypotheses.content: The recorded m92 loading-solvent feature may matter, but the EA-versus-PE association is not yet reproducible enough to support a broad solvent correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched EA measurements at new strength and loading levels can teach whether solvent identity contributes a stable signal or is confounded by endpoint and measurement variation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the EA-loaded m92 response at 100 ul form a consistent strength trend relative to the earlier EA and PE records?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl-containing and hydrogen-bonding scaffolds require separate onset and finish calibration. Tertiary alcohol, phenol, and hydroxyester records do not support a common shift for all alcohol-containing molecules.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected m203 and m51 local curves distinguish growth of onset from growth of finish and constrain transfer across different hydrogen-bonding environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m203 and m51 intermediate points preserve their different interval-width behavior across loading and solvent strength?

hypotheses.content: A subset of aromatic carbonyl, nitro, nitrile, and multifunctional molecules occupies a long-tail regime that is substantially underrepresented by the model; the regime is chemically selective rather than explained by a single polarity descriptor.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Novel high-CW-distance structures and lower-strength anchors can improve tail calibration while reducing extrapolation of long-tail corrections into ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural motifs and condition ranges reliably place molecules into the long-tail regime, and which only produce isolated outliers?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes strengthen the view that response curves must be scaffold specific. m75 changed from 18.43/30.51 at 20/1 and 50 ul to 5.55/11.63 at 50/1 and 50 ul, but at 150 ul the same ratio change gave 15.84/31.84 to 37.94/51.52 (3726956d81fe3954e5b7; 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e; e35fdc08a1113b193889; 9249ed2c527f70995033). This supports targeted intermediate m75 measurements rather than a universal monotonic rule. m25, m164, and m53 each showed substantial weak-eluent growth across matched or near-matched conditions (74701496b6fc5465eea7; c9bef93a79964dc6ede1; 6e17f8e15aa8fdd6a9ea; 6e17f8e15aa8fdd6a9ea), supporting local curve repair for carbonyl-rich scaffolds. m203 did not preserve its compact 150-ul finish at 50 ul: the 20/1 observations were 31.00/34.93 at 150 ul and 37.76/44.96 at 50 ul, while 10/1 and 150 ul was 12.97/22.33 (66747ae127e03516ffda; 9ed7c1fb1c2cc499bbf9; 04ea307c7b7f3321cc20). m51 showed strong fixed-loading growth from 5/1 to 10/1 (bf09d868ed4d68a97b40; 4fb92bd1fab3ba235858), motivating lower-strength anchors. m92 EA and PE records remain variable enough that the solvent effect is unresolved, so the batch uses independent EA replicates. The latest m81 replicate supported short finishes but did not eliminate endpoint variation, motivating one more intermediate-loading point. The unusual m117 regimes failed to recur consistently, so they receive no further slot here.
batch_rationale: The batch repairs several local failure regions while preserving chemical coverage. The m75, m203, m92, m81, and m51 selections are linked experiments that discriminate loading, solvent, onset, and finish hypotheses. m25, m53, m94, and m95 extend response curves where measured weak-eluent growth is already evident. The m157, m155, m214, m52, m136, m152, m3, and m208 rows add structurally distinct molecules, including donor-free halogenated and polyaryl systems, so retraining can learn beyond the heavily sampled carbonyl families. The remaining aldehyde, amino-ester, nitro, ester, and aromatic points test whether observed long-tail or hydroxyl-associated behavior transfers across related functional environments. Together, the measurements cover ordinary compact regimes, steep response transitions, high-retention tails, and condition-sensitive exceptions across the Row-distribution, improving graph-condition interactions and reducing broad corrections driven by isolated historical errors.
